Produce expert findings now. The full bundle is attached via relevant_files: the diff, both candidate source files, the RELEASED provider baseline source + its provenance manifest, the python review criteria, and the feature design/implementation/tasks docs.

Review target = candidate client.py + tests/test_client.py. Criteria = the python checklists + functional-review + change-context + scope protocols. Intent = the enhanced-settings design docs.

Central analysis required — trace the compatibility combination mandated by the design's hard constraint "preserving independently releasable main":
- New client (candidate) sends {"settings": values, "require_receipt": True} and raises RuntimeError("Provider did not acknowledge applied settings") unless response.get("applied") is True.
- The released provider (baseline, what main must stay compatible with until Task 2 ships in the separate provider repo) returns {"ok": True} with NO "applied" key.
- Therefore, if this client increment is released on main on its own (as the hard requirement demands, and Task 2 is still pending), every ordinary save against the currently-released provider now raises RuntimeError. The design also states ordinary saves must continue to work and the enhanced UI is disabled by default — yet the receipt is required unconditionally, not gated behind enhanced_settings (which remains an unused passthrough).
- Also assess: the unit test was edited so its fake provider returns applied:True — evaluate whether that masks the regression and whether any test still covers the released-provider response shape.

Determine severity and whether the increment satisfies independently-releasable-main. Identify inspected coverage and any unresolved comparisons. Report correctness, security, architecture/design-intent and quality findings in your native format with severities.
